근거 ❾ · 해석: 인간은 여전히 다른 사람들과 조화롭게 행동하지만, 본성보다는 양육에 의해 더 형성된 패턴을 통해서이다.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) rejects — (B) consideration — (C) unrelated
(A) supports — (B) neglect — (C) central
(A) rejects — (B) neglect — (C) unrelated
(A) rejects — (B) consideration — (C) central
(A) supports — (B) consideration — (C) unrelated
choice.ex: (A) rejects (B) consideration (C) unrelated 근거 ❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❸ does not rank animals by likeness to humans = 순위 매기기를 거부함 / (B) ❹ has concern for ~ as much as = 배려 / (C) ❺ the human form of life is simply irrelevant = 관련 없는. supports(지지하다)는 ❸ does not rank와 정반대, neglect(무시)는 concern과 반대, central(중 심적인)은 irrelevant와 정반대. 요약문 해석: CA는 동물들이 얼마나 인간 같은지에 따라 그들의 순위를 매기는 것을 (A) 거부한다. 그것은 핀치와 돼지에게 고래와 코끼리만큼의 (B) 배려 를 주는데, 인간의 삶의 방식은 다른 종이 필요로 하는 것과 (C) 관련이 없기 때문이다.
choice.psg: ❶ What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it? ❷ It is easy to say what it is not. ❸ The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches. ❹ The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant. ❺ And it argues that the human form of life is simply irrelevant when we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves. ❻ What is relevant is their own forms of life. ❼ Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. ❽ We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. ❾ According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.
choice.body: The CA (A)________ ranking animals according to how human-like they are; it gives the finch and the pig as much (B)________ as the whale and the elephant, because the human way of life is (C)________ to what other species need.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) distinctively — (B) suited — (C) compete
(A) barely — (B) suited — (C) thrive
(A) distinctively — (B) suited — (C) thrive
(A) barely — (B) foreign — (C) compete
(A) distinctively — (B) foreign — (C) thrive
choice.ex: (A) distinctively (B) suited (C) thrive 근거 ❼❾ 해설: (A) ❼ the characteristic goods of a human life = 독특하게 인간다운 / (B) ❼ a finch seeks a finch’s life, ❾ characteristic for that creature = 자기 종에 알맞은 / (C) ❾ the opportunity to flourish = 번성하다. barely(간신히)는 characteristic의 의미가 아님, foreign(낯선)은 ‘고유 한’과 반대, compete(경쟁하다)는 flourish가 아님. 요약문 해석: 인간이 (A) 독특하게 인간다운 삶을 추구하는 것처럼, 지각 있는 모든 존재는 자기 종류에 (B) 알맞은 삶을 추구하므로, 우리는 각 생명체에 게 그 삶의 형태로 (C) 번성할 기회를 주어야 한다.
choice.psg: ❶ What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it? ❷ It is easy to say what it is not. ❸ The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches. ❹ The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant. ❺ And it argues that the human form of life is simply irrelevant when we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves. ❻ What is relevant is their own forms of life. ❼ Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. ❽ We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. ❾ According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.
choice.body: Just as humans pursue a (A)________ human life, every sentient being seeks a life (B)________ to its own kind, so we should give each creature the chance to (C)________ in that form of life.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: The CA differs from views that favor human-like animals.
The CA argues that humans should give up their own way of life to protect animals.
Humans should make an effort to learn about how other creatures live.
What each animal needs should be judged by its own way of living.
The CA treats small animals with the same concern as large ones.
choice.ex: 본문은 인간의 삶의 형태가 동물의 필요를 판단하는 데 무관하다(❺)고 할 뿐, 인간이 자신의 삶의 방식을 포기해야 한다는 주장은 없 음(오히려 ❼ 인간도 인간다운 삶을 추구함을 인정). 작은 동물에 대한 같은 관심은 ❹, 고유한 삶의 방식으로 판단은 ❺❻, 다른 생명체에 대해 배우려는 노력은 ❽, 인간 같은 동물을 우대하는 관점과의 차이는 ❸에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❸ — CA는 인간과 비슷한 동물을 우대하는 관점들과 다르다. ② 근거 없음(정답) — CA는 인간이 동물을 보호하기 위해 자신의 삶의 방식을 포기해야 한다고 주장한다. ③ 근거 ❽ — 인간은 다른 생명체들이 어떻게 사는지 배우려고 노력해야 한다. ④ 근거 ❺❻ — 각 동물에게 필요한 것은 그 동물 자신의 삶의 방식으로 판단되어야 한다. ⑤ 근거 ❹ — CA는 작은 동물을 큰 동물과 같은 관심으로 대한다.
choice.psg: ❶ What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it? ❷ It is easy to say what it is not. ❸ The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches. ❹ The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant. ❺ And it argues that the human form of life is simply irrelevant when we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves. ❻ What is relevant is their own forms of life. ❼ Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. ❽ We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. ❾ According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: treat animals as more important than people in every case
spend too little time watching animals in zoos
believe that lazy animals deserve less care from humans
draw pictures of animals without proper artistic training
carelessly assume that animals are just weaker versions of people who want what we want
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 우리는 스스로를 확장하고 배워야 하며, 동물들을 열등한 인간으로, 우리와 같은 식의 삶을 추구한다고 성의 없이 상상해서 는 안 된다. 해설: 밑줄 뒤 ‘seeking a life sort of like our own(우리와 같은 식의 삶을 추구한다고)’이 풀이를 줌 → 동물을 우리와 같은 것을 원하는 열등한 인간쯤으 로 안이하게 여기는 것. 그림을 그린다는 것은 picture를 글자 그대로 읽은 함정, 동물을 사람보다 중요하게 대한다는 것은 본문에 없는 과장, 동물원 관찰 은 무관, lazy를 동물의 성격으로 읽은 것은 오독. ① 모든 경우에 동물을 사람보다 더 중요하게 대하다 ② 동물원에서 동물을 관찰하는 데 너무 적은 시간을 쓰다 ③ 게으른 동물은 인간에게서 더 적은 보살핌을 받아야 한다고 믿다 ④ 제대로 된 미술 훈련 없이 동물 그림을 그리다 ⑤ 동물을 우리가 원하는 것을 원하는 더 약한 인간쯤으로 안이하게 가정하다
choice.body: Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.
choice.ul: lazily picture animals as lesser humans,

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) vaguely — (B) hide — (C) weakens
(A) reliably — (B) review — (C) strengthens
(A) reliably — (B) hide — (C) strengthens
(A) vaguely — (B) review — (C) strengthens
(A) reliably — (B) review — (C) weakens
choice.ex: (A) reliably (B) review (C) strengthens 근거 ❷❸ 해설: (A) ❷ better remembered and less forgotten = 확실하게 / (B) ❸ rehearse(되풀이하다) = 되짚어 보다 / (C) ❸ facilitating long-term memory retention = 강화하다. vaguely(희미하게)는 better remembered와 반대, hide(숨기다)는 공유·되풀이와 반대, weakens는 facilitating과 정 반대. 요약문 해석: 사람들이 온라인에 게시한 사건은 그 성격과 관계없이 게시하지 않은 사건보다 더 (A) 확실하게 회상되는데, 아마 공유가 사람들로 하여금 그 사건을 (B) 되짚어 보고 해석하게 하여 장기 기억을 (C) 강화하기 때문일 것이다.
choice.psg: ❶ Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering. ❷ Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events. ❸ This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention. ❹ Online feedback such as comments and likes as well as technological features such as algorithms and periodic reminders can further serve as memory cues for the posted event details. ❺ As a result, event details shared on social media are likely stabilized and remembered over time, whereas those not shared may become inaccessible or forgotten.
choice.body: Events that people post online are recalled more (A)________ than unposted ones, regardless of their nature, possibly because sharing lets people (B)________ and interpret them, which (C)________ long-term memory.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) prompts — (B) persist — (C) fade
(A) prompts — (B) persist — (C) sharpen
(A) obstacles — (B) persist — (C) fade
(A) obstacles — (B) vanish — (C) sharpen
(A) prompts — (B) vanish — (C) fade
choice.ex: (A) prompts (B) persist (C) fade 근거 ❹❺ 해설: (A) ❹ can further serve as memory cues = (기억을 떠올리게 하는) 자극제 / (B) ❺ stabilized and remembered over time = 지속되다 / (C) ❺ may become inaccessible or forgotten = 희미해지다. obstacles(장애물)는 cues와 반대, vanish(사라지다)는 stabilized와 반대, sharpen(선명 해지다)은 forgotten과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 다른 사람들의 반응과 알고리즘 같은 도구는 사람들이 게시된 세부 사항을 떠올리도록 돕는 (A) 자극제로 작용하므로, 공유된 기억은 시간이 지나도 (B) 지속되는 경향이 있는 반면 공유되지 않은 기억은 (C) 희미해질 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering. ❷ Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events. ❸ This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention. ❹ Online feedback such as comments and likes as well as technological features such as algorithms and periodic reminders can further serve as memory cues for the posted event details. ❺ As a result, event details shared on social media are likely stabilized and remembered over time, whereas those not shared may become inaccessible or forgotten.
choice.body: Responses from others and tools like algorithms act as (A)________ that help people recall posted details, so shared memories tend to (B)________ over time while unshared ones may (C)________.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Memories that are never shared online may be lost more easily.
Thinking about past events again may help keep them in memory.
People’s responses to a post can help bring back memories of it.
Posting about an event can make it easier to remember later.
People who post often online have better memories in general than people who do not.
choice.ex: 본문은 ‘게시된 사건’이 ‘게시되지 않은 사건’보다 더 잘 기억된다는 것(사건 단위 비교)일 뿐, 자주 게시하는 사람이 전반적인 기억력 자체가 좋다는 것(사람 단위 비교)은 말하지 않음(과잉 일반화). 게시하면 기억하기 쉬움은 ❷, 다시 생각하기(rehearse)의 효과는 ❸, 반응이 기억을 되살림은 ❹, 공유되지 않은 기억의 소실은 ❺에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❺ — 온라인에 전혀 공유되지 않은 기억은 더 쉽게 잃어버릴 수 있다. ② 근거 ❸ — 지난 사건을 다시 생각하는 것은 그것을 기억 속에 유지하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❹ — 게시물에 대한 사람들의 반응은 그것에 대한 기억을 되살리는 데 도움이 될 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❷ — 어떤 사건에 대해 게시하는 것은 나중에 그것을 기억하기 더 쉽게 만들 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 온라인에 자주 게시하는 사람들은 그렇지 않은 사람들보다 전반적으로 기억력이 더 좋다.
choice.psg: ❶ Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering. ❷ Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events. ❸ This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention. ❹ Online feedback such as comments and likes as well as technological features such as algorithms and periodic reminders can further serve as memory cues for the posted event details. ❺ As a result, event details shared on social media are likely stabilized and remembered over time, whereas those not shared may become inaccessible or forgotten.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: because the events had nothing to do with the person
unless the events were shared only with close friends
only when the events were exciting or unusual
no matter what kind of experience was posted
as long as the person posted them without any help
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 소셜 미디어 플랫폼에 게시된 개인적 사건들은 그 사건들의 특성과 무관하게, 게시되지 않은 것들보다 더 잘 기억되고 덜 잊 힌다. 해설: ‘사건의 특성과 무관하게’ → 사건이 어떤 종류(중요·사소, 즐거움·슬픔 등)이든 게시 여부가 기억에 영향을 준다는 뜻. 흥미진진하거나 특이할 때만이 라는 것은 정반대, 사람과 관련이 없다는 것은 independent를 잘못 읽은 함정, 도움 없이 게시·친한 친구와의 공유 조건은 본문에 없음. ① 그 사건들이 그 사람과 아무 관련이 없었기 때문에 ② 그 사건들이 친한 친구들하고만 공유되지 않는다면 ③ 사건이 흥미진진하거나 특이할 때에만 ④ 어떤 종류의 경험이 게시되었는지와 상관없이 ⑤ 그 사람이 아무 도움 없이 그것들을 게시하기만 한다면
choice.body: Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering. Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events. This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention.
choice.ul: independent of the characteristics of the events.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) treasure — (B) combination — (C) purely
(A) overlook — (B) combination — (C) purely
(A) overlook — (B) separation — (C) purely
(A) treasure — (B) separation — (C) partly
(A) overlook — (B) combination — (C) partly
choice.ex: (A) overlook (B) combination (C) purely 근거 ❶❷❹❺ 해설: (A) ❶ we often take them for granted = 간과하다 / (B) ❹ a fusion of the senses = 결합 / (C) ❺ We first eat with our eyes, but ~ also ~ countless sensory signals = 순전히 시각적인 것이 아님. treasure(소중히 여기다)는 ‘당연하게 여긴다’와 반대, separation(분리)은 fusion과 반대, partly(부분적으로)는 시각도 실제로 식사 경험의 일부(❺ eat with our eyes)이므로 ‘~이 아니라’와 모순. 요약문 해석: 우리는 보통 다중 감각 경험을 (A) 간과하지만, 먹는 것 같은 일상 활동조차 살펴보면 그것이 (C) 순전히 시각적인 경험이 아니라 여러 감각 의 (B) 결합임을 알 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses. ❷ However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. ❸ Consider the experience of eating a regular meal. ❹ At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. ❺ We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells. ❻ And it does not stop there. ❼ Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.
choice.body: Although we usually (A)________ our multisensory experiences, examining even an everyday activity such as eating shows that it is a (B)________ of many senses rather than a (C)________ visual experience.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) surroundings — (B) do not affect — (C) perceive
(A) thoughts — (B) shape — (C) perceive
(A) surroundings — (B) shape — (C) perceive

choice.ex: 본문은 안경으로 교정된 감각을 당연하게 여긴다(❶)고 했을 뿐, 시력이 식사의 즐거움을 좌우한다는 비교는 없음(본문 밖 비교). 평범 한 경험의 다중 감각은 ❷❹, 잘 작동할 때 알아차리지 못함은 ❶, 도구의 역할은 ❼, 보는 것이 식사의 일부임은 ❺에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❶ — 우리는 감각이 잘 작동할 때 얼마나 많은 감각을 쓰는지 거의 알아차리지 못한다. ② 근거 ❷❹ — 우리가 평범하다고 생각하는 경험도 동시에 많은 감각을 포함할 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❼ — 먹는 데 쓰는 도구는 식사가 경험되는 방식에 한몫할 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❺ — 음식을 보는 것은 식사 경험의 일부이다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 시력이 나쁜 사람들은 시력이 좋은 사람들보다 식사를 덜 즐긴다.

choice.ex: (A) isolated (B) naturally (C) forward 근거 ❷❹❻ 해설: (A) ❷ perceive words ~ separately from each other = 분리된 / (B) ❻ not automatically turn to the right = 자연스럽게(저절로) / (C) ❻ continue riding straight ahead = 앞으로. linked는 ❷와 반대, gladly(기꺼이)는 automatically의 의미가 아님, backward(뒤로)는 straight ahead와 반대. 요약문 해석: 어린아이들은 각 단어를 다른 단어들과 (A) 분리된 것으로 다루기 때문에 ‘오른쪽’이 ‘왼쪽’의 반대라는 것을 (B) 자연스럽게 깨닫지 못한다. 왼쪽으로 가지 말라는 말을 들은 아이는 그저 (C) 앞으로 계속 나아갈 수도 있다.

read.ko: 능력 접근법(CA)이란 무엇이며, 동물 정의에 열정을 가진 법률가들이 왜 그것에 관심을 가질까?
read.en: What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it?

read.ko: 그것이 아닌 것을 말하는 것이 쉽다.
read.en: It is easy to say what it is not.

read.ko: CA는 다른 널리 퍼진 이론적 접근들이 그러하듯, 동물들을 인간과의 유사성에 따라 순위를 매기거나 가장 ‘우리와 비슷한’ 존재로 여겨지는 동물에게 각별 한 특권을 부여하려 하지 않는다.
read.en: The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches.

read.ko: CA는 고래와 코끼리에게만큼이나 핀치와 돼지에게도 관심을 가진다.
read.en: The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant.

read.ko: 그리고 그것은 우리가 각 종류의 동물이 필요로 하고 마땅히 누려야 할 것에 대해 생각할 때, 인간의 삶의 형태는 그저 무관하다고 주장한다.
read.en: And it argues that the human form of life is simply irrelevant when we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves.

read.ko: 관련이 있는 것은 ‘그들 고유의’ 삶의 형태이다.
read.en: What is relevant is their own forms of life.

read.ko: 꼭 인간이 인간다운 삶의 고유한 좋은 것들을 누릴 수 있기를 추구하는 것처럼, 핀치는 핀치의 삶을, 고래는 고래의 삶을 추구한다.
read.en: Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life.

read.ko: 우리는 스스로를 확장하고 배워야 하며, 동물들을 열등한 인간으로, 우리와 같은 식의 삶을 추구한다고 성의 없이 상상해서는 안 된다.
read.en: We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own.

read.ko: CA에 따르면, 지각 능력이 있는 각각의 생명체는 그 생명체에게 고유한 삶의 형태로 번영할 기회를 가져야 한다.
read.en: According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.

read.ko: 소셜 미디어는 자전적 기억을 촉진하는 중요한 맥락으로 작용한다.
read.en: Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering.

read.ko: 소셜 미디어 플랫폼에 게시된 개인적 사건들은 그 사건들의 특성과 무관하게, 게시되지 않은 것들보다 더 잘 기억되고 덜 잊힌다.
read.en: Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events.

read.ko: 이것은 온라인에서 기억을 공유하는 것이 개인이 일어난 일을 되풀이하고 이해하도록 해서 장기 기억 유지를 촉진하기 때문일 수 있다.
read.en: This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention.

read.ko: 알고리즘과 주기적인 알림과 같은 기술적 기능들뿐만 아니라, 댓글과 좋아요와 같은 온라인 피드백도 게시된 사건의 세부 사항에 대한 기억 단서로 한층 더 작용할 수 있다.
read.en: Online feedback such as comments and likes as well as technological features such as algorithms and periodic reminders can further serve as memory cues for the posted event details.

read.en: Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses.

read.en: However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live.

read.ko: 일상의 식사를 하는 경험을 생각해 봐라.
read.en: Consider the experience of eating a regular meal.

read.ko: 처음에는, 그것이 평범한 경험처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제로 그것은 감각들의 융합이다.
read.en: At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses.

read.ko: 우리는 처음에는 눈으로 식사하지만, 또한 음식의 질감, 맛, 냄새와 같이 우리의 식사 경험에 영향을 미치는 수많은 감각 신호에도 노출된다.
read.en: We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells.

read.ko: 그리고 그것은 거기서 멈추지 않는다.

read.en: Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.

read.ko: 어릴 때, 반대의 원리는 낯설다.
read.en: As children, the principle of opposites is foreign.

read.ko: 아이들은 단어들과 그 의미들을 서로 분리해서 인식한다.
read.en: Children perceive words and their meanings separately from each other.

read.ko: 우리가 개별 단어들이 직접적으로 서로 연결되어 있다는 것을 이해하게 되는 것은 나중의 발달 단계가 되어서이다.
read.en: It is only in later development that we understood that individual words directly connect to one another.

read.ko: 예를 들어, 많은 아이들에게, ‘오른쪽’이 ‘왼쪽’의 반대라는 것은 분명하지 않다.
read.en: For many children, for instance, it is not clear that ‘Right’ is the opposite of ‘Left’.

read.ko: 이것의 생생한 사례는 아이들이 자전거 타는 것을 배울 때 보여질 수 있다.
read.en: A vivid example of this can be seen when children learn to ride a bicycle.

read.ko: 부모들이 자녀에게 “왼쪽으로 가지 마.”라고 말하면, 부모는 아이가 곧장 앞으로 계속 가고 자동적으로 오른쪽으로 방향을 틀지 않는 것을 종종 보게 될 것 이다.
read.en: If parents tell their child “Don’t go to the left,” they will often find that the child will continue riding straight ahead and not automatically turn to the right.

read.ko: 같은 원리가 부모가 인식하는 ‘예’와 ‘아니요’ 사이의 논리적 관계에도 적용된다.
read.en: The same applies to the logical connection between ‘Yes’ and ‘No’ as perceived by parents.

read.ko: 우리가 아이였을 때, 예를 들어, “안 돼, 손으로 먹지 마.”라는 말을 들었을 때, 우리는 혼란스러웠고, 우리 부모가 우리로부터 기대하는 것이 무엇인지 몰랐 다.
read.en: When we were children and were told, for example, “No, don’t eat with your hands,” we were confused and didn’t know what our parents expected from us.

read.ko: 우리의 혼란은 계속 먹어야 하는 건지 아닌지, 만약 먹는다면 어떻게 해야 하지?에 대한 것이었다.
read.en: Our confusion was about whether we should continue eating or not and if so, how?

read.ko: 나중에서야 우리는 그 연관성을 인식했고, 우리가 손이 아니라 포크나 숟가락으로 계속 먹어야 한다는 것을 이해하게 되었다.
read.en: Only later did we recognize the connection and understand that we should continue eating, but not with our hands but with a fork or a spoon.

read.ko: 인간이 ‘가장’ 사회적인 동물은 아니다.
read.en: Humans are not the most social animal.

read.ko: 개미, 벌, 그리고 흰개미는 많은 사회성 측정 기준에서 인류를 부끄럽게 한다.
read.en: Ants, bees, and termites put humanity to shame on many metrics of sociality.

read.ko: 매우 다양한 동족들이 완벽하게 조화로운 행동으로 함께 살고 집단적으로 그들의 어린 새끼들을 돌본다.
read.en: A wide variety of relatives live together with perfectly harmonious behavior and collectively care for their young.

read.ko: 그러나 곤충 군집들이 인상적으로 사회적인 장소인 반면, 그것은 ‘우리의’ 사회생활의 종류가 아니다.
read.en: But while insect colonies are impressively social places, it’s not our kind of social life.

read.ko: 벌들은 항상 육각형의 벌집을 짓고, 개미들은 줄지어 행진하며, 흰개미들은 지그재그 대형으로 움직인다.
read.en: Bees always build hexagonal hives, ants march in lines, and termites move in zigzag formations.

read.ko: 이러한 패턴들은 그것들이 유전적으로 긴밀하게 프로그램되어 있으며 페로몬에 의해 추진되기 때문에 예측할 수 있게 반복된다.
read.en: These patterns recur predictably because they are tightly programmed genetically and propelled pheromonally.

read.ko: 우리 인간은 더 자유롭고, 유전적으로 덜 긴밀하게 프로그램되어 있어서 우리의 사회적 패턴들은 더 다양하고 역동적일 수 있다.
read.en: We humans are more free, less tightly programmed genetically, so our social patterns can be more diverse and dynamic.

read.ko: 모든 집단은 약간 다른 춤을 추는데 이러한 안무들은 세대에 걸쳐 변한다.
read.en: Every group dances a slightly different dance, and these choreographies change across generations.

read.ko: 우리는 여전히 우리 주변의 다른 사람들과 조화를 이루는 방식으로 생각하고 행동하지만, 그것은 단지 본성만이 아니라 양육에 의해 더 많이 형성되는 패 턴들을 통해서이다.
read.en: We still think and act in ways that are in harmony with others around us, but it is through patterns that are more shaped by nurture, not just nature.

para.en: What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it? It is easy to say what it is not. The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches. The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant. And it argues that the human form of life is simply irrelevant when we think about what each type of animal needs and deserves. What is relevant is their own forms of life. Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. According to the CA, each sentient creature should have the opportunity to flourish in the form of life characteristic for that creature.

Social media serves as an important context to facilitate autobiographical remembering. Personal events posted on social media platforms are better remembered and less forgotten than those not posted, independent of the characteristics of the events. This may be because sharing memories online allows individuals to rehearse and make sense of what happened, thus facilitating long-term memory retention. Online feedback such as comments and likes as well as technological features such as algorithms and periodic reminders can further serve as memory cues for the posted event details. As a result, event details shared on social media are likely stabilized and remembered over time, whereas those not shared may become inaccessible or forgotten.

Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses. However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. Consider the experience of eating a regular meal. At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells. And it does not stop there. Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.

As children, the principle of opposites is foreign. Children perceive words and their meanings separately from each other. It is only in later development that we understood that individual words directly connect to one another. For many children, for instance, it is not clear that ‘Right’ is the opposite of ‘Left’. A vivid example of this can be seen when children learn to ride a bicycle. If parents tell their child “Don’t go to the left,” they will often find that the child will continue riding straight ahead and not automatically turn to the right. The same applies to the logical connection between ‘Yes’ and ‘No’ as perceived by parents. When we were children and were told, for example, “No, don’t eat with your hands,” we were confused and didn’t know what our parents expected from us. Our confusion was about whether we should continue eating or not and if so, how? Only later did we recognize the connection and understand that we should continue eating, but not with our hands but with a fork or a spoon.

Humans are not the most social animal. Ants, bees, and termites put humanity to shame on many metrics of sociality. A wide variety of relatives live together with perfectly harmonious behavior and collectively care for their young. But while insect colonies are impressively social places, it’s not our kind of social life. Bees always build hexagonal hives, ants march in lines, and termites move in zigzag formations. These patterns recur predictably because they are tightly programmed genetically and propelled pheromonally. We humans are more free, less tightly programmed genetically, so our social patterns can be more diverse and dynamic. Every group dances a slightly different dance, and these choreographies change across generations. We still think and act in ways that are in harmony with others around us, but it is through patterns that are more shaped by nurture, not just nature.
